intro: You already guess with must, might and can't, about now and about the past. Today you add finer shades: will for confident assumptions (That'll be the courier), be bound to, be likely to and be supposed to for how sure or how expected something is, and could have and would have for things that didn't happen.
teachingNotes: Recap in two lines, don't re-teach: from b1-modals-deduction-present and b2-modals-deduction the learner knows must / might / can't be (guesses about now) and must / might / can't have + third form (guesses about the past), plus needn't have done (did it, wasn't necessary) vs didn't need to do (not necessary, usually not done); should have (seharusnya) comes from b2-wish-regrets and would / could have + third form from b2-third-conditional. Go further: the new tools are will / won't for assumptions, be bound / likely / supposed to, and the fine meanings of could have and would have without an if-part.

will / won't + base verb for a confident assumption about NOW, not the future (objective will-for-assumptions): 'The doorbell! That'll be the courier' (= pasti kurirnya tuh), 'She won't be at home now, she works till six', 'Don't call him now, he'll be driving' (will be + -ing), and, as a note, will have + third form for the past ('They'll have landed by now'). will is based on what you know (routines, timetables, habits); must is a conclusion from evidence. They often both work (That'll be / That must be the courier): never test will vs must as the only difference. Test meaning (now, not future) and form (keep be: not 'That'll the courier'; not 'She won't at home'). Indonesian trap: pasti covers must, will and bound to; and learners read will as 'akan' every time.

be bound to / be likely to / be supposed to + base verb (objective bound-likely-supposed). bound to = almost certain, often from experience (It's bound to rain in Bogor in January; He's bound to be late, he always is) = pasti (deh). likely / unlikely to = probable / improbable (kemungkinan besar / kecil kemungkinannya); also It is likely that + clause (It's likely that prices will rise); likely is an adjective here, and American English also uses it as an adverb (He'll likely be late), where British English prefers probably / most likely. supposed to = expected by a rule, plan, arrangement or what people say, and often NOT happening (seharusnya / mestinya menurut aturan / rencana): We're supposed to finish by Friday (but we won't); not supposed to = not allowed, softer than mustn't (You're not supposed to park here); It's supposed to be a great film = katanya; was supposed to = planned but didn't happen. Common errors: *'He is bound to coming late' -> 'bound to come' (to here is followed by the base verb, like want to); *'We are supposed to finished by Friday' -> 'supposed to finish'; *'suppose to' (the d isn't heard in speech, but it's written: supposed to). Don't test supposed to vs should (should can also express expectation); test meaning: certain vs probable vs expected by a plan or rule.

Past modals with fine meaning (objective past-modal-nuance): could have + third form = it was possible but didn't happen (We could have taken the toll road; You could have been hurt!) and criticism (You could have told me! = kamu kan bisa bilang). would have + third form = an imagined result or willingness that didn't happen, the third conditional without its if-part spoken (I would have helped, but nobody asked = he didn't help; She would have loved this place). could = it was possible / there was a chance; would = it was what I wanted or what would certainly have happened. Recap needn't have done vs didn't need to do in one line, and the common error *'I needn't have to bring an umbrella' -> 'I needn't have brought an umbrella' (or 'I didn't have to bring one'): needn't is already the helper, so no have to, and needn't have + third form. couldn't have + comparative (I couldn't have asked for a better team) can be shown as a phrase to remember.

C1 honesty: many choices here are about nuance, and several forms can be right (That'll be / That must be; could have / should have for criticism; didn't need to can also be used when it was done). Only test clear cases where the context makes one meaning clearly right, and accept the natural alternative where the rubric says so. Contractions: that'll, she'll, won't, could've, would've, I'd have; never write 'could of / would of'.

Limits: no inversion, cleft sentences, subjunctive or impersonal passives (It is said that ...): for 'katanya' teach It's supposed to be ..., not passive reporting. No should for probability as a taught point, no shall, no dare / ought to. Contexts: offices and ministries in Jakarta, campuses in Yogyakarta and Bandung, startups and NGOs, KRL / MRT, ojek online, couriers, rupiah, international partners.

keyPoints.title: will / won't for confident assumptions about now
keyPoints.explanation: will / won't + base verb can be a confident assumption about NOW, based on what you know (routines, timetables, habits), not a future event: That'll be the courier. She won't be at home now, she works till six. With -ing for something in progress now: He'll be driving. It's close to must be, but will sounds like 'I know how things usually are'. Keep be: not 'That'll the courier'.

examples.en: The doorbell! That'll be the courier.
She won't be at home now. She works till six.
examples.id: Dia pasti tidak di rumah sekarang. Dia kerja sampai jam enam.

examples.en: Don't call Pak Hasan now. He'll be driving to the office.
examples.id: Jangan telepon Pak Hasan sekarang. Dia pasti sedang menyetir ke kantor.

id.title: will / won't untuk asumsi yang yakin tentang sekarang
id.explanation: will / won't + kata kerja dasar bisa berarti asumsi yang yakin tentang SEKARANG, berdasarkan apa yang kamu tahu (kebiasaan, jadwal), bukan kejadian di masa depan: That'll be the courier (pasti kurirnya). She won't be at home now, she works till six. Dengan -ing untuk sesuatu yang sedang berlangsung: He'll be driving (pasti sedang menyetir). Mirip must be, tapi will terdengar seperti 'aku tahu biasanya begitu'. Jangan hilangkan be: bukan 'That'll the courier'.

keyPoints.title: be bound to, be likely to, be supposed to
keyPoints.explanation: All three take to + the base verb (bound to come, not 'bound to coming'; supposed to finish, not 'supposed to finished'). be bound to = almost certain (It's bound to rain). be likely / unlikely to = probable / improbable (Prices are likely to rise; also It's likely that prices will rise). be supposed to = expected by a rule, a plan or what people say, and often it doesn't happen (We're supposed to finish by Friday; You're not supposed to park here; It's supposed to be a great film).

examples.en: It's January in Bogor. It's bound to rain this afternoon.
examples.id: Ini bulan Januari di Bogor. Sore ini pasti hujan.

examples.en: The minister is unlikely to resign before the election.
examples.id: Kecil kemungkinannya menteri itu mundur sebelum pemilu.

examples.en: We're supposed to finish the report by Friday, but the data isn't ready.
examples.id: Menurut rencana, kita seharusnya menyelesaikan laporan itu hari Jumat, tapi datanya belum siap.

id.title: be bound to, be likely to, be supposed to
id.explanation: Ketiganya diikuti to + kata kerja dasar (bound to come, bukan 'bound to coming'; supposed to finish, bukan 'supposed to finished'). be bound to = hampir pasti (It's bound to rain). be likely / unlikely to = kemungkinan besar / kecil kemungkinannya (Prices are likely to rise; juga It's likely that prices will rise). be supposed to = seharusnya menurut aturan, rencana, atau kata orang, dan sering tidak terjadi (We're supposed to finish by Friday; You're not supposed to park here = tidak boleh parkir di sini; It's supposed to be a great film = katanya filmnya bagus).

keyPoints.title: could have, would have, needn't have, didn't need to
keyPoints.explanation: All four talk about the past, and the first two are about things that did NOT happen. could have + third form = it was possible, but it didn't happen (You could have been hurt!), or criticism (You could have told me! = kamu kan bisa bilang). would have + third form = what you were willing to do or what would certainly have happened, but didn't (I would have helped, but nobody asked). Recap: needn't have + third form = you did it, but it wasn't necessary; didn't need to + base verb = not necessary, usually not done. Not 'needn't have to bring': say needn't have brought.

examples.en: You could have told me the meeting was cancelled!
examples.id: Kamu kan bisa bilang ke aku kalau rapatnya dibatalkan!

examples.en: I would have helped, but nobody asked.
examples.id: Aku sebenarnya mau membantu, tapi tidak ada yang minta.

examples.en: We needn't have hurried. The client was late too.
examples.id: Ternyata kita tidak perlu buru-buru (padahal sudah). Kliennya juga terlambat.

id.title: could have, would have, needn't have, didn't need to
id.explanation: Keempatnya tentang masa lalu, dan dua yang pertama tentang hal yang TIDAK terjadi. could have + bentuk ketiga = waktu itu mungkin / bisa, tapi tidak terjadi (You could have been hurt! = kamu bisa saja terluka!), atau kritik (You could have told me! = kamu kan bisa bilang). would have + bentuk ketiga = yang sebenarnya kamu mau lakukan, atau yang pasti akan terjadi, tapi tidak terjadi (I would have helped, but nobody asked = aku sebenarnya mau bantu, tapi tidak ada yang minta). Ulasan: needn't have + bentuk ketiga = sudah dilakukan, tapi ternyata tidak perlu; didn't need to + kata kerja dasar = tidak perlu, biasanya tidak dilakukan. Bukan 'needn't have to bring': bilang needn't have brought.

guidedPractice.prompt: It's 10 am on a Tuesday. Sari teaches a class every weekday morning. Complete with will be + teach: Don't call Sari now. She ___ her morning class.
expected: 'll be teaching
will be teaching
she'll be teaching her morning class
she will be teaching her morning class
guidedPractice.hint: A confident assumption about something in progress now: will be + -ing.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: Don't lend Budi your charger. He's bound to losing it.
expected: he's bound to lose it
he is bound to lose it
don't lend budi your charger he's bound to lose it
guidedPractice.hint: be bound to + the base verb, like want to: bound to lose.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with be supposed to + leave: The flight to Medan ___ at 8:00, but it's been delayed until 10:30.
expected: was supposed to leave
is supposed to leave
the flight to medan was supposed to leave at 8:00
the flight to medan is supposed to leave at 8:00
guidedPractice.hint: The plan says 8:00, but it isn't happening: is / was supposed to + base verb.

guidedPractice.prompt: Rewrite with It is likely that: Interest rates are likely to rise next month.
expected: it is likely that interest rates will rise next month
it's likely that interest rates will rise next month
guidedPractice.hint: It is likely that + a full sentence (subject + will + verb).

guidedPractice.prompt: Rina climbed onto a wobbly office chair to change a light bulb. Complete with could have + fall: That was dangerous! You ___.
expected: could have fallen
could've fallen
you could have fallen
you could've fallen
guidedPractice.hint: It was possible, but it didn't happen: could have + the third form (fallen).

independentPractice.prompt: Think of three people you know. Where are they right now, and what are they doing? Write one confident assumption with will or won't for each.
expected: my mother will be at home now she'll be cooking
budi won't be at the office he works from home on fridays
my sister will be in class now
independentPractice.hint: will / won't + be + place, or will be + -ing: about now, not the future.

independentPractice.prompt: Write about one plan at your office or campus: what is supposed to happen, and how likely is it to happen on time? Use supposed to and bound to, likely to or unlikely to.
expected: the new system is supposed to start in march but it's unlikely to be ready
we're supposed to move offices next month and it's bound to be chaotic
independentPractice.hint: supposed to = the plan; bound to / likely to / unlikely to = how sure you are.

independentPractice.prompt: Write two true sentences about last year: one with could have (a chance you didn't take) and one with would have (something you wanted to do, but it didn't happen).
expected: i could have taken a job in surabaya i would have gone to bali but the flights were too expensive
i could have studied more i would have joined the trip but i was ill
independentPractice.hint: could have = it was possible; would have = you were willing, but it didn't happen.

assessment.prompt: It's 12:15 and your phone is ringing. Your manager, Pak Hasan, calls you every day at lunchtime to check on the project. Write the missing word: That'll ___ Pak Hasan.
assessment.rubric: Correct: be (That'll be Pak Hasan = a confident assumption about now: pasti Pak Hasan). 'is' = 20 (will is always followed by the base verb). Leaving the gap empty or adding another verb = 0.

assessment.prompt: It's 3 pm on a Wednesday. Rina wants to drop off a package at Bu Ani's house. You know Bu Ani works at the ministry until five every weekday. Complete with will or won't: She ___ be at home now. Try her office.
acceptableAnswers: she won't be at home now
she will not be at home now
assessment.rubric: Correct: won't / will not (a confident assumption about now, based on her routine: pasti tidak di rumah). 'will' = 0 (the opposite meaning). Writing 'can't' = 60 (a correct deduction, but the item asks for will or won't). 'won't at home' (no be) = 50.

assessment.prompt: Dimas has been late for every Monday meeting this year. Complete with the right form of come: He's bound to ___ late again next Monday.
acceptableAnswers: he's bound to come late again next monday
he is bound to come late again next monday
assessment.rubric: Correct: come (be bound to + base verb = almost certain). 'coming' = 20 (the common error: to here is followed by the base verb). 'came' = 10. 'be late' instead of come = 70 (correct English, but the item asks for come).

assessment.prompt: Read this news summary: 'Under the government's plan, the new MRT line will open in 2027. However, construction is already eight months behind schedule.' Complete with bound, likely or supposed: The new MRT line is ___ to open in 2027.
acceptableAnswers: the new mrt line is supposed to open in 2027
assessment.rubric: Correct: supposed (supposed to = expected by a plan, and it may not happen: menurut rencana seharusnya). 'likely' = 20 (the text suggests delays, so it's not clearly probable). 'bound' = 0 (almost certain: the opposite of the text). 'suppose' = 70 (the d is silent in speech but must be written).

assessment.prompt: Bu Ani's daughter collects batik, but she was in Makassar during the big batik exhibition in Yogyakarta. Bu Ani says: 'She ___ loved it.' Complete with could have or would have.
assessment.rubric: Correct: would have / would've / 'd have (an imagined result that didn't happen: she wasn't there, but she certainly would have loved it). 'could have' = 30 (could is about possibility or a chance, which doesn't fit loving something). 'would of' = 60 (spelling: write would have or would've).

assessment.prompt: Your housemate used your laptop without asking and spilled coffee on the keyboard. You say: 'You ___ asked me first!' Complete with could have or would have.
acceptableAnswers: you could have asked me first
assessment.rubric: Correct: could have / could've (criticism: it was possible, but he didn't do it: kamu kan bisa minta izin dulu). 'should have' = 80 (also natural criticism, but the item asks for could have or would have). 'would have' = 20 (that's an assumption about what he would have done, not a complaint). 'could of' = 60 (spelling).

assessment.prompt: At the airport you bought ten bottles of water for your team. At the hotel in Surabaya, every room had free water. Complete with the right form of buy: We needn't have ___ so much water.
acceptableAnswers: we needn't have bought so much water
we need not have bought so much water
assessment.rubric: Correct: bought (needn't have + third form = you did it, but it wasn't necessary). 'buy' = 30 (third form needed). 'brought' = 40 (a different verb: bring). 'to buy' = 10 (not 'needn't have to').

material.title: That'll be the courier: will about now

blocks.text:
**Quick recap:** you already guess with **must / might / can't be** (about now) and **must / might / can't have + the third form** (about the past). You also know **needn't have done** vs **didn't need to do**.

Today's first new tool: **will / won't + base verb** for a **confident assumption about now**. It's not about the future at all:
- *The doorbell! **That'll be** the courier.* = Pasti kurirnya tuh.
- *She **won't be** at home now. She works till six.* = Pasti dia tidak di rumah sekarang.

The assumption comes from **what you know**: routines, timetables, habits. You ordered something, the courier usually comes around now, so: *That'll be the courier.*
For something **in progress now**, use **will be + -ing**: *Don't call him now, he**'ll be driving**.* (pasti sedang menyetir)

id.text:
**Ulasan singkat:** kamu sudah bisa menduga dengan **must / might / can't be** (tentang sekarang) dan **must / might / can't have + bentuk ketiga** (tentang masa lalu). Kamu juga tahu **needn't have done** vs **didn't need to do**.

Alat baru pertama hari ini: **will / won't + kata kerja dasar** untuk **asumsi yang yakin tentang sekarang**. Ini sama sekali bukan tentang masa depan:
- *The doorbell! **That'll be** the courier.* = Pasti kurirnya tuh.
- *She **won't be** at home now. She works till six.* = Pasti dia tidak di rumah sekarang.

Asumsinya datang dari **apa yang kamu tahu**: kebiasaan, jadwal, rutinitas. Kamu memesan barang, kurir biasanya datang jam segini, jadi: *That'll be the courier.*
Untuk sesuatu yang **sedang berlangsung sekarang**, pakai **will be + -ing**: *Don't call him now, he**'ll be driving**.* (pasti sedang menyetir)

rows.en: The doorbell! That'll be the courier.
rows.id: Bel pintu! Pasti kurirnya tuh.
rows.note: now, not future: the courier is at the door

id.note: sekarang, bukan masa depan: kurirnya sudah di depan pintu

rows.en: She won't be at home now. She works till six.
rows.id: Dia pasti tidak di rumah sekarang. Dia kerja sampai jam enam.

rows.en: Don't call Pak Hasan now. He'll be driving to the office.
rows.id: Jangan telepon Pak Hasan sekarang. Dia pasti sedang menyetir ke kantor.

rows.en: You'll be tired after such a long flight. Sit down.
rows.id: Kamu pasti capek setelah penerbangan sepanjang itu. Duduklah.

rows.en: It's eight o'clock in Jakarta. Their plane will have landed by now.
rows.id: Sudah jam delapan di Jakarta. Pesawat mereka pasti sudah mendarat sekarang.
rows.note: will have + third form = an assumption about something already done

id.note: will have + bentuk ketiga = asumsi tentang sesuatu yang sudah terjadi

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap: will isn't always 'akan'.** You learnt *will* as the future, so *That'll be the courier* can look like 'kurirnya akan datang'. Here it means **pasti** (I'm confident it's true now). And keep **be**: Indonesian has no *to be*, so learners write 'That'll the courier' or 'She won't at home'. Say **That'll be**, **She won't be**.
**will or must?** *That'll be the courier* and *That must be the courier* are both correct and very close. *must* sounds like a conclusion from evidence (I can see a delivery van); *will* sounds like 'I know how things usually are'. Don't worry about choosing between them: both are fine.
**Not for the future:** for a prediction about tomorrow, *pasti* is **will definitely** or **be bound to** (next section), not *must*: *He must be late* means 'pasti dia sudah telat' (now).

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: will tidak selalu 'akan'.** Kamu belajar *will* sebagai bentuk masa depan, jadi *That'll be the courier* bisa terlihat seperti 'kurirnya akan datang'. Di sini artinya **pasti** (aku yakin itu benar sekarang). Dan jangan hilangkan **be**: bahasa Indonesia tidak punya *to be*, jadi orang menulis 'That'll the courier' atau 'She won't at home'. Bilang **That'll be**, **She won't be**.
**will atau must?** *That'll be the courier* dan *That must be the courier* sama-sama benar dan sangat mirip. *must* terdengar seperti kesimpulan dari bukti (aku melihat mobil pengiriman); *will* terdengar seperti 'aku tahu biasanya begitu'. Tidak usah pusing memilih: dua-duanya benar.
**Bukan untuk masa depan:** untuk prediksi tentang besok, *pasti* = **will definitely** atau **be bound to** (bagian berikutnya), bukan *must*: *He must be late* artinya 'pasti dia sudah telat' (sekarang).

blocks.prompt: It's 1 pm. A colleague asks where Sari is. Sari has lunch at the warung across the street every day at one. Choose the best reply.
options: She's going to the warung tomorrow.
blocks.explain: A confident assumption about now, from her routine → will + be: She'll be at the warung. 'She'll at the warung' drops be, and the third option is about tomorrow, not now.

id.prompt: Jam 1 siang. Seorang rekan kerja bertanya Sari di mana. Sari makan siang di warung seberang jalan setiap hari jam satu. Pilih jawaban terbaik.
id.explain: Asumsi yang yakin tentang sekarang, dari kebiasaannya → will + be: She'll be at the warung. 'She'll at the warung' tidak memakai be, dan pilihan ketiga tentang besok, bukan sekarang.

material.title: How sure? be bound to and be likely to

blocks.text:
Two phrases say **how sure** you are that something will happen (or is generally true). Both are **be + word + to + base verb**:
- **be bound to** = almost certain, often from experience → *pasti (deh)*.
*It's January in Bogor. It's **bound to rain** this afternoon.* *Don't worry, you're **bound to find** a job with your experience.*
- **be likely to** = probable → *kemungkinan besar*. **be unlikely to** = probably not → *kecil kemungkinannya*.
*Prices are **likely to rise** after Lebaran.* *The minister is **unlikely to resign**.*
**It is likely that** + a full sentence means the same: *It's **likely that** prices **will rise** after Lebaran.*
From most sure to least: **bound to** → **likely to** → **unlikely to**.

id.text:
Dua frasa ini menyatakan **seberapa yakin** kamu bahwa sesuatu akan terjadi (atau umumnya benar). Keduanya berpola **be + kata + to + kata kerja dasar**:
- **be bound to** = hampir pasti, sering dari pengalaman → *pasti (deh)*.
*It's January in Bogor. It's **bound to rain** this afternoon.* *Don't worry, you're **bound to find** a job with your experience.*
- **be likely to** = kemungkinan besar. **be unlikely to** = kecil kemungkinannya.
*Prices are **likely to rise** after Lebaran.* *The minister is **unlikely to resign**.*
**It is likely that** + kalimat lengkap artinya sama: *It's **likely that** prices **will rise** after Lebaran.*
Dari paling yakin ke paling tidak yakin: **bound to** → **likely to** → **unlikely to**.

rows.en: He's bound to be late. He always is.
rows.id: Dia pasti telat deh. Dia selalu telat.

rows.en: With your experience, you're bound to find a job.
rows.id: Dengan pengalamanmu, kamu pasti dapat kerja.

rows.en: Prices are likely to rise after Lebaran.
rows.id: Harga kemungkinan besar naik setelah Lebaran.

rows.en: It's likely that the meeting will move online.
rows.id: Kemungkinan besar rapatnya pindah ke online.
rows.note: It is likely that + subject + will + verb

id.note: It is likely that + subjek + will + kata kerja

rows.en: The minister is unlikely to resign before the election.
rows.id: Kecil kemungkinannya menteri itu mundur sebelum pemilu.

blocks.text:
**Form trap: to + the base verb.** The *to* here works like *want to*: the base verb comes next. Not 'He is bound to coming late' → **He is bound to come late**. Not 'likely to rising' → **likely to rise**. And don't drop *be*: not 'Prices likely to rise' in a normal sentence (news headlines drop it, but sentences don't) → **Prices are likely to rise**.
**British vs American:** Americans also use *likely* like *probably*: *He'll likely be late.* In British English, *He'll probably be late* or *He's likely to be late* is more usual (*most likely* works in both).
**bound to vs must:** both can translate *pasti*, but *He's bound to be late* is a prediction (he isn't late yet), and *He must be late* is a conclusion about now (he's late already).

id.text:
**Jebakan bentuk: to + kata kerja dasar.** *to* di sini bekerja seperti *want to*: sesudahnya kata kerja dasar. Bukan 'He is bound to coming late' → **He is bound to come late**. Bukan 'likely to rising' → **likely to rise**. Dan jangan hilangkan *be*: bukan 'Prices likely to rise' dalam kalimat biasa (judul berita menghilangkannya, kalimat biasa tidak) → **Prices are likely to rise**.
**Inggris vs Amerika:** orang Amerika juga memakai *likely* seperti *probably*: *He'll likely be late.* Dalam bahasa Inggris British, *He'll probably be late* atau *He's likely to be late* lebih umum (*most likely* dipakai di keduanya).
**bound to vs must:** dua-duanya bisa berarti *pasti*, tapi *He's bound to be late* adalah prediksi (dia belum telat), sedangkan *He must be late* adalah kesimpulan tentang sekarang (dia sudah telat).

blocks.prompt: A weather app says: 70% chance of rain in Jakarta tomorrow. Which sentence matches it best?
blocks.explain: 70% = probable, but not almost certain → likely to rain. bound to sounds almost 100% sure, and unlikely to means it probably won't rain.

id.prompt: Aplikasi cuaca bilang: 70% kemungkinan hujan di Jakarta besok. Kalimat mana yang paling cocok?
id.explain: 70% = kemungkinan besar, tapi belum hampir pasti → likely to rain. bound to terdengar hampir 100% yakin, dan unlikely to berarti kemungkinan besar tidak hujan.

id.title: Seberapa yakin? be bound to dan be likely to

material.title: be supposed to: the plan, the rule, what people say

blocks.text:
**be supposed to + base verb** is not about how sure you are. It's about what is **expected** by a **plan, a rule, an arrangement** or **what people say**. Very often, the reality is different. Learn **supposed to** as a fixed phrase: it looks like a passive, but you don't need to analyse it.
- **a plan** (often not happening): *We**'re supposed to finish** by Friday, but the data isn't ready.*
- **a past plan that didn't happen**: *The train **was supposed to leave** at 7:00.* (it didn't)
- **a rule** (negative = not allowed, softer than *mustn't*): *You**'re not supposed to park** here.*
- **what people say**: *It**'s supposed to be** a great film.* = Katanya filmnya bagus.

id.text:
**be supposed to + kata kerja dasar** bukan tentang seberapa yakin kamu. Ini tentang apa yang **diharapkan** oleh **rencana, aturan, kesepakatan** atau **kata orang**. Sering sekali, kenyataannya berbeda. Hafalkan **supposed to** sebagai frasa tetap: bentuknya mirip pasif, tapi tidak perlu dianalisis.
- **rencana** (sering tidak terjadi): *We**'re supposed to finish** by Friday, but the data isn't ready.* = Menurut rencana kita seharusnya selesai hari Jumat, tapi datanya belum siap.
- **rencana di masa lalu yang tidak terjadi**: *The train **was supposed to leave** at 7:00.* (ternyata tidak)
- **aturan** (bentuk negatif = tidak boleh, lebih halus daripada *mustn't*): *You**'re not supposed to park** here.*
- **kata orang**: *It**'s supposed to be** a great film.* = Katanya filmnya bagus.

rows.en: We're supposed to finish the report by Friday, but the data isn't ready.
rows.id: Menurut rencana, kita seharusnya menyelesaikan laporan itu hari Jumat, tapi datanya belum siap.

rows.en: The train was supposed to leave at seven. It left at half past eight.
rows.id: Keretanya seharusnya berangkat jam tujuh. Ternyata berangkat jam setengah sembilan.
rows.note: half past eight = 8:30 (in Indonesian: setengah sembilan)

rows.en: You're not supposed to smoke in this building.
rows.id: Tidak boleh merokok di gedung ini.

rows.en: That new ramen place in Bandung is supposed to be excellent.
rows.id: Katanya restoran ramen baru di Bandung itu enak sekali.

rows.en: What are we supposed to bring to the workshop?
rows.id: Kita seharusnya bawa apa ke workshop-nya?

blocks.text:
**Form traps:**
- **to + base verb**: not 'We are supposed to finished by Friday' → **We are supposed to finish by Friday**.
- **Spelling:** in speech the *d* disappears ('su-POHS-tu'), so learners write 'suppose to'. Write **supposed to**.
- **be** changes, *supposed* doesn't: *I'm / she's / they were supposed to*.
**The Indonesian trap: seharusnya.** *Seharusnya* can be *should* (advice or opinion: *You should rest*) or *supposed to* (a plan or rule from outside). If it's about a timetable, a deadline, an agreement or a rule, and especially if things went wrong, **supposed to** is the natural choice.
**katanya** about something you haven't tried yourself = **It's supposed to be …**

id.text:
**Jebakan bentuk:**
- **to + kata kerja dasar**: bukan 'We are supposed to finished by Friday' → **We are supposed to finish by Friday**.
- **Ejaan:** saat diucapkan, bunyi *d* hilang ('su-POHS-tu'), jadi banyak yang menulis 'suppose to'. Tulis **supposed to**.
- yang berubah **be**, *supposed* tidak: *I'm / she's / they were supposed to*.
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: seharusnya.** *Seharusnya* bisa berarti *should* (saran atau pendapat: *You should rest*) atau *supposed to* (rencana atau aturan dari luar). Kalau tentang jadwal, tenggat, kesepakatan atau aturan, apalagi kalau ternyata tidak berjalan sesuai rencana, **supposed to** adalah pilihan yang wajar.
**katanya** tentang sesuatu yang belum kamu coba sendiri = **It's supposed to be …**

blocks.prompt: Budi tells you: 'I was supposed to fly to Bali this morning.' What do you understand?
options: He flew to Bali this morning, as planned.
He planned to fly to Bali, but it didn't happen.
He will probably fly to Bali later today.
blocks.explain: was supposed to = it was the plan, and it usually means it didn't happen (something went wrong). If he had flown, he'd simply say 'I flew to Bali this morning'.

id.prompt: Budi bilang padamu: 'I was supposed to fly to Bali this morning.' Apa yang kamu pahami?
id.explain: was supposed to = itu rencananya, dan biasanya artinya tidak terjadi (ada masalah). Kalau dia jadi terbang, dia cukup bilang 'I flew to Bali this morning'.
options: Dia terbang ke Bali pagi ini sesuai rencana.
Dia berencana terbang ke Bali, tetapi tidak jadi.
Dia mungkin terbang ke Bali nanti hari ini.

material.title: could have, would have, needn't have

blocks.text:
**Recap:** *must / might / can't have done* = guesses about the past; *should have done* = seharusnya (regret or criticism); *needn't have done* = you did it, but it wasn't necessary; *didn't need to do* = not necessary, usually not done.

Two more, both about things that **didn't happen**:
- **could have + third form** = it was **possible**, there was a chance, but it didn't happen. *We **could have taken** the toll road, but we chose the old road.* *Be careful! You **could have been** hurt!*
  Also **criticism**: *You **could have told** me!* = kamu kan bisa bilang! (you didn't)
- **would have + third form** = what you were **willing** to do, or what would **certainly** have happened, but didn't. It's the third conditional with the *if*-part left out. *I **would have helped**, but nobody asked.* (I didn't help) *Sari **would have loved** this concert.* (she isn't here)
In speech: **could've, would've, I'd have**. Never write 'could of' or 'would of'.

id.text:
**Ulasan:** *must / might / can't have done* = dugaan tentang masa lalu; *should have done* = seharusnya (penyesalan atau kritik); *needn't have done* = sudah dilakukan, tapi ternyata tidak perlu; *didn't need to do* = tidak perlu, biasanya tidak dilakukan.

Dua lagi, keduanya tentang hal yang **tidak terjadi**:
- **could have + bentuk ketiga** = waktu itu **mungkin / bisa**, ada kesempatan, tapi tidak terjadi. *We **could have taken** the toll road, but we chose the old road.* (kita bisa saja lewat tol) *Be careful! You **could have been** hurt!* (kamu bisa saja terluka!)
  Juga untuk **kritik**: *You **could have told** me!* = kamu kan bisa bilang! (tapi tidak)
- **would have + bentuk ketiga** = yang sebenarnya kamu **mau** lakukan, atau yang **pasti** akan terjadi, tapi tidak terjadi. Ini third conditional tanpa bagian *if*. *I **would have helped**, but nobody asked.* (aku tidak membantu) *Sari **would have loved** this concert.* (Sari tidak ada di sini, tapi dia pasti suka)
Saat diucapkan: **could've, would've, I'd have**. Jangan pernah menulis 'could of' atau 'would of'.

rows.en: We could have taken the toll road, but we chose the old road.
rows.id: Kita bisa saja lewat tol, tapi kita memilih jalan lama.
rows.note: could have = a possibility that didn't happen

id.note: could have = kemungkinan yang tidak terjadi

rows.en: You could have told me the meeting was cancelled!
rows.id: Kamu kan bisa bilang ke aku kalau rapatnya dibatalkan!

rows.en: I would have helped, but nobody asked.
rows.id: Aku sebenarnya mau membantu, tapi tidak ada yang minta.
rows.note: would have = willing, but it didn't happen

id.note: would have = sebenarnya mau, tapi tidak terjadi

rows.en: I'd have called you, but my phone died.
rows.id: Tadinya aku mau meneleponmu, tapi HP-ku mati.

rows.en: I couldn't have done it without you.
rows.id: Aku tidak mungkin bisa melakukannya tanpamu.
rows.note: a phrase to remember for thanking someone

id.note: frasa untuk berterima kasih, hafalkan saja

blocks.text:
**could have or would have?** Ask: was it **possible**, or was it **wanted / certain**?
- *I **could have** helped* = I was able to (I was free, I had the skills).
- *I **would have** helped* = I was willing to (I wanted to, if someone had asked).
Both say it **didn't happen**. In Indonesian, *bisa saja* / *kan bisa* points to **could have**; *sebenarnya mau* / *pasti akan* points to **would have**.
**The needn't trap:** not 'I needn't have to bring an umbrella'. *needn't* is already the helper word, so it can't take *have to*. Say **I needn't have brought an umbrella** (I brought it, for nothing) or **I didn't have to bring an umbrella** (= didn't need to).

id.text:
**could have atau would have?** Tanyakan: apakah itu **mungkin / bisa**, atau **diinginkan / pasti**?
- *I **could have** helped* = aku sebenarnya bisa (waktunya ada, kemampuannya ada).
- *I **would have** helped* = aku sebenarnya mau (kalau ada yang minta).
Dua-duanya berarti **tidak terjadi**. Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *bisa saja* / *kan bisa* mengarah ke **could have**; *sebenarnya mau* / *pasti akan* mengarah ke **would have**.
**Jebakan needn't:** bukan 'I needn't have to bring an umbrella'. *needn't* sudah merupakan kata bantu, jadi tidak bisa ditambah *have to*. Bilang **I needn't have brought an umbrella** (sudah bawa, ternyata sia-sia) atau **I didn't have to bring an umbrella** (= didn't need to).

blocks.prompt: Pak Hasan drove home from Puncak at 80 km/h in heavy rain. His wife says: 'That was dangerous! You ___ an accident.' Choose the best option.
blocks.explain: An accident was possible, but it didn't happen → could have had. would have had would mean an accident was certain (or wanted), and needn't have had means he had one, but it wasn't necessary.

id.prompt: Pak Hasan menyetir pulang dari Puncak dengan kecepatan 80 km/jam di tengah hujan deras. Istrinya bilang: 'That was dangerous! You ___ an accident.' Pilih yang paling tepat.
id.explain: Kecelakaan itu mungkin terjadi, tapi tidak terjadi → could have had. would have had berarti kecelakaan itu pasti (atau diinginkan), dan needn't have had berarti dia sudah kecelakaan, tapi tidak perlu.

id.intro: Kamu sudah bisa menduga dengan must, might dan can't, tentang sekarang dan tentang masa lalu. Hari ini kamu menambah nuansa yang lebih halus: will untuk asumsi yang yakin (That'll be the courier = pasti kurirnya tuh), be bound to, be likely to dan be supposed to untuk seberapa yakin atau seberapa diharapkan sesuatu, serta could have dan would have untuk hal-hal yang tidak terjadi.
suggestedQuestions: Apakah 'That'll be the courier' tentang masa depan?
Apa bedanya bound to dan likely to?
Kapan saya pakai supposed to, bukan should?
Apa bedanya 'I could have helped' dan 'I would have helped'?

assessment.mn-1: Jam 12.15 dan teleponmu berdering. Manajermu, Pak Hasan, meneleponmu setiap hari saat makan siang untuk mengecek proyek. Tulis kata yang hilang: That'll ___ Pak Hasan.
assessment.mn-2: Jam 3 sore hari Rabu. Rina mau mengantar paket ke rumah Bu Ani. Kamu tahu Bu Ani bekerja di kementerian sampai jam lima setiap hari kerja. Lengkapi dengan will atau won't: She ___ be at home now. Try her office.
assessment.mn-3: Dimas selalu terlambat di setiap rapat hari Senin tahun ini. Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang benar dari come: He's bound to ___ late again next Monday.
assessment.mn-4: Baca ringkasan berita ini: 'Under the government's plan, the new MRT line will open in 2027. However, construction is already eight months behind schedule.' Lengkapi dengan bound, likely atau supposed: The new MRT line is ___ to open in 2027.
assessment.mn-5: Putri Bu Ani mengoleksi batik, tapi dia sedang di Makassar waktu ada pameran batik besar di Yogyakarta. Bu Ani bilang: 'She ___ loved it.' Lengkapi dengan could have atau would have.
assessment.mn-6: Teman serumahmu memakai laptopmu tanpa izin dan menumpahkan kopi ke keyboard-nya. Kamu bilang: 'You ___ asked me first!' Lengkapi dengan could have atau would have.
assessment.mn-7: Di bandara kamu membeli sepuluh botol air untuk timmu. Di hotel di Surabaya, setiap kamar ternyata punya air gratis. Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang benar dari buy: We needn't have ___ so much water.
